_comment: Fixed regression corpus for the extraction pipeline. Selected from documents that already have a human-verified final_human_annotation/instances_default.json (real ParcelMap region locations, not guessed). Document content is land-record data and stays out of git per repo policy -- this file only records IDs and known behavior, never document text/images.

documents.why_included: 5-parcel stacked shared-edge case (pages 6-8). Known open issue: Parcel 1 area comes out ~50% off. Included to track whether future changes make this better, worse, or don't touch it.
documents.known_baseline_notes: Confirmed recoverable overall but Parcel 1 accuracy miss was left open as of KNOWN_ISSUES.md.

documents.why_included: Known duplicate-region-detection issue (same parcel enumerated twice across a batch boundary). Low priority but real; corpus should show if a future batching change fixes or worsens it.
Real 7-call self-intersecting traverse. Used to verify find_self_intersecting_segment_pair keeps correctly naming the crossing edges (call 1 x call 6) as prompts/geometry code change.
documents.known_baseline_notes: As of 6f45e4f: self-intersection message correctly names call 1 and call 6.

documents.why_included: Region 5 / page 8 was rerun 15-20x this session to measure real success rate under non-determinism -- already has a rough base-rate reference point. Good canary for batching/enumeration regressions.
documents.known_baseline_notes: Base success rate measured this session; exact figure lives in scratch_diag/ (gitignored) -- rerun to refresh before trusting it as a hard baseline.

documents.why_included: Small, simple document where the OCR-grounded structuring experiment showed a real WIN. Keep in corpus so any future OCR work has to prove it doesn't regress this too.
documents.known_baseline_notes: OCR-integration test: improved here. Vision-only pipeline baseline should be captured fresh.

documents.why_included: The OCR-grounded structuring experiment TOTALLY FAILED here. This is the single most important regression canary in the corpus -- any future OCR/structuring change must be run against this document first.
documents.known_baseline_notes: OCR-integration test: total failure. Vision-only pipeline baseline should be captured fresh.

documents.why_included: Sparse case -- only one ParcelMap region across 29 pages. Tests that the pipeline doesn't over-enumerate or hallucinate regions on mostly-text documents.
documents.known_baseline_notes: Not deeply tested this session -- first real baseline run will establish it.

documents.why_included: Small, simple, 2-region document -- fast canary for quick sanity checks between larger runs.
documents.known_baseline_notes: Not deeply tested this session -- first real baseline run will establish it.

documents.why_included: Largest ParcelMap-region density in the corpus (74 regions). Stress test for batching/enumeration at scale, where over-enumeration and duplicate-label bugs are most likely to surface.
documents.known_baseline_notes: Not deeply tested this session -- first real baseline run will establish it.

documents.why_included: Largest document by page count in the corpus. Tests pipeline behavior (timeouts, batching, memory) at the far end of document size.
documents.known_baseline_notes: Not deeply tested this session -- first real baseline run will establish it.

not_yet_added.nvz_placerville: WTPM26-0004_Placerville_app.pdf (the tie-line / Track-B / curly-quote document this whole session centered on) should be in this corpus too, but its document-id in data/documents/ wasn't confirmed against the UUIDs above before writing this file -- don't guess it, confirm it (e.g. by grepping page text for 'NVZ LLC' or '352.40') and add it as a normal entry before the first baseline run.
